notice: Light news day — fewer fresh items than usual.

lead.title: Karpathy turns a Lord of the Rings paragraph into a playable Three.js world with Opus 5
lead.summary: Karpathy handed Opus 5 a ~1M-token / ~$10 budget with the opening of The Lord of the Rings, and the model spent roughly two hours writing 5,500+ lines of Three.js to procedurally render and animate the story, self-correcting via screenshots. A playable browser version was published, spotlighting long-horizon agentic creative coding.

top_stories.title: Nous Research: Hermes Agent gains traction as a high-performing open-source agent
top_stories.summary: Nous Research highlights growing buzz around Hermes Agent, with observers calling it 'insanely good' and betting the team can build a large company if execution holds.

top_stories.title: Simon Willison surfaces under-discovered ChatGPT Work features: built-in browser and Cloudflare Workers deploy
top_stories.summary: Willison notes ChatGPT Work (mobile/web mode) ships an integrated browser with screenshots and can deploy web apps straight to Cloudflare Workers ('ChatGPT Sites'), with discoverability the main remaining gap.

top_stories.title: Nous Portal offers DeepSeek V4 Flash at 90% off for 7 days
top_stories.summary: Nous Research promotes DeepSeek V4 Flash at 90% off via novita_labs, claiming it outperforms a top model on Terminal-Bench 2.1 while being over 1,000x cheaper, with other models 20-50% off — a fresh salvo in inference pricing.

top_stories.title: Karpathy expands on agentic long-context coding limits
top_stories.summary: Following the LoTR demo, Karpathy notes LLMs shine at ambitious long-horizon coding tasks humans avoid but still struggle to self-audit visual and gameplay output without slow screenshot loops, linking to Simon Willison's 'pelican on a bicycle' testing idea.

items.title: WCM: A World Critic Model for Vision-Language-Action Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Adds a future-state value estimator on top of VLA backbones to improve RL post-training for robotic manipulation, beating single-frame value-based baselines.

items.title: The Parts Are Greater Than the Sum: automated task sequencing for multi-policy LLMs
items.summary: Sequences heterogeneous tasks to reduce interference and catastrophic forgetting in shared low-rank adapter fine-tuning, improving transfer and retention over naive shared-LoRA.

items.title: ExtractBench: a benchmark for schema-guided enterprise document extraction
items.summary: Evaluates agents on following a user-defined schema with source evidence grounding for enterprise document workflows.

items.title: DungeonBench: rules-rich tactical reasoning in D&D combat
items.summary: A benchmark where geometry, timing, resources and rule interactions all matter, turning decisions into measurable outcomes to stress-test models beyond typical game benchmarks.

items.title: AMTFV: agentic mathematical tool-flow verification for LLM self-correction
items.summary: Verifies candidate answers via tool-flow rather than natural-language reflection only, improving answer verification and self-correction over reflection-only baselines.

items.title: mlxsh — serve multiple local LLMs on Apple Silicon
items.summary: A lightweight CLI that serves several local LLMs on Apple hardware via the MLX stack.

items.title: OpenTalking — privately deployable real-time AI avatar
items.summary: A self-hostable real-time avatar for on-premises talking-face and avatar apps without cloud dependencies.

items.title: gnt — a company brain AI agents check before acting
items.summary: An open-source system giving agents a shared company-wide knowledge base to consult before acting.

items.title: Zizq — fast single-binary job queue
items.summary: A lightweight, single-binary job queue designed to drop into any stack with minimal setup.

items.title: AI Visibility — check if ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini recommend your brand
items.summary: A web tool that checks whether major AI assistants recommend your brand in their responses, for marketers and founders tracking AI referral visibility.
